abstract: Let $S,S'$ be very general K3 surfaces of degrees $2s^2d$ and $2d$ ($s\ge2$) whose transcendental lattices are rationally but not integrally Hodge isometric, as in rStation paper 132. That paper showed that the integral Hodge conjecture (IHC) on $S\times S'^b$, $b\le19$, is equivalent to the algebraicity of a cross class $\varphi$ with $\varphi|_T=s\iota$, and asked about $\varphi$ and triple classes $\xi_p$ on $S\times S\times S'$. We prove that $\varphi$ is algebraic: a twisted derived equivalence $D^b(S)\simeq D^b(S',\alpha')$, with $\alpha'$ of order $s$, untwisted by a twisted sheaf, puts the Brauer order exactly on $\varphi$. So IHC holds on $S\times S'^b$ for $b\le19$. A third Chern character shows that $2\xi_s$ is algebraic, and $\xi_s$ is algebraic for odd $s$, so IHC holds on $S\times S\times S'$ for odd $s$. On $S^2\times S'^2$ a new integral class $\eta$ appears (exact Smith normal forms, $d=1$, $s=2,3,5,7$). Modulo the other classes, $\eta$ is detected by the coefficient of one crossing matching of transcendental parts, and this explains why two natural families of kernel products do not reach it. For the first family this is equivalent to an index gap: $\alpha'\boxtimes\alpha'$ on $S'\times S'$ has period $s$ and index $s^2$. For $s=2$ this index gap gives, by Hotchkiss's method, a Severi–Brauer sevenfold over $S'\times S'$ on which IHC fails in degree 6. For $\gcd(s,6)=1$, Perry's categorical IHC for $D^b(S^2\times S'^2)$ would imply that $\eta$ is algebraic. Whether $\eta$ is algebraic is left open.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary:
Version 2 makes the clarity and bibliographic changes requested in the version 1 report and adds an explanation (formula (4.1)) of why the two kernel families of Proposition 4.2 miss eta. No theorem or proposition statement changes. An earlier version 2 submission (g--1zuhyJTxNKmto) was rejected for scope; following that report, its abelian-surface Remark 4.5, the generalizations of Propositions 4.2 and 5.1, Remark 4.6 and the related supplement folders (qa/, ssp2.py, pairs.py, sigma.py) are removed here and will be presented in a separate paper citing this one.
1. References: the mnemonic labels are replaced by numbered references [1]-[14] in order of first citation, each with an arXiv or rStation URL. Huybrechts [13] (arXiv:2411.17604, Thm 0.4) and Bottini-Huybrechts [14] (arXiv:2512.15131, Thms B-D) are cited in Remark 5.4 as context for period-index bounds on hyperkähler varieties.
2. Section 4, opening: compact definitions of the pairwise subring A, of A^+, and of Sat for a Künneth component, so that Proposition 4.1 no longer relies on [3] for them.
3. Proposition 4.2: separates the rational expression u.x/epsilon printed by the scripts from its use mod s. The proof now records that u.x is an integer and that only (u.x) epsilon^{-1} in Z/s enters. The scripts print u and epsilon (supplement eta2.py; each eta3_s*.out and etaQ_s*.out gains one line, otherwise identical to version 1).
4. Theorem D: spells out the normalization of Q. If Q_0 = 2H + pi^*l, comparison with -K_{P/X} shows that f - l is an integral (1,1) class, so a line-bundle twist gives Q = 2H + pi^*f.
5. Introduction: the vanishing of the topological (Atiyah-Hirzebruch and cobordism) obstructions is attributed to even, torsion-free cohomology together with the integrality of the Chern character on these products [6], not to torsion-freeness alone.
6. Section 4, definition of Sat: the parenthetical 'rationally A spans every Hodge class here' is restricted to the components considered (fewer than 21 factors, so no SO(T) determinant invariants).
7. Abstract: the computational detail is shortened and the explanation by (4.1) is added (238 words).
8. Supplement: eta2.out, eta3.out, etaQ.out regenerated with the new u line (the eta3_s4/etaQ_s4 files still record the mod-4 exception); reproduce.sh uses pipefail and lists its dependencies; the unused [Muk] reference is dropped.
9. Introduction and Remark 5.4: the scope of the index argument is stated precisely. The rank divisibility s^2 persists on higher powers and Hilbert schemes of S', but by (4.1) it is equivalent to lambda = 0 only for the first family of Proposition 4.2; the second family is excluded because its crossing coefficient is a product of two ranks divisible by s.
10. Corrections to Sections 1 and 4: the B-field normalization of v(P), v(Q) in Proposition 4.2 is stated; ch tensor Q is called an isomorphism of rational Hodge structures (not a Hodge isometry); [Sat : A^+ + Z eta] = 1 is stated in Proposition 4.1, and the five-factor computation is labelled a model computation; the ranges of Theorems A-C are stated in the introduction.
11. New formula (4.1) in the proof of Proposition 4.2: for d = 1, s = 2, 3, 5, 7 and x in Sat, lambda(x) = mu_13(x)/s = -mu_14(x)/s mod s, where mu_13, mu_14 are the coefficients of the crossing matchings iota_13 iota_24, iota_14 iota_23 in the transcendental part (they lie in s^2 Z on A^+, and equal s, -s on eta). This gives a script-free proof of Proposition 4.2 (same statement) in the true lattice: the first family has mu_14 = 0, the second has mu_14 = +-rr' with s | r, r'. It also recovers s^2 | rk Q (Proposition 5.1) from integrality, and in Question 4.3 it replaces the Lambda^2 invariant, which did not separate eta at s = 2 (at s = 2 the new coefficient detects generators of Sat/A^+, but A^+ is not known to be algebraic there). The introduction, abstract and Remark 5.4 now attribute the failure of the tested families to (4.1) rather than to the index. New script matching.py (outputs matching_s{2,3,5,7}.out) checks the coefficients on the generators of A^+, on eta and symbolically on both families; the earlier scripts etaQ.py, eta3.py remain as an independent check.
title: The cross class of isogenous K3 surfaces is algebraic, and an index gap on S'×S'
